headline: Tigers in control: Bangladesh lead by 67 runs with 6 wickets left in Darwin Test
summary: Bangladesh holds a commanding position after three days of play, leaving Australia struggling to recover from a 228-run first-innings lead.
details: Bangladesh is firmly in control of the first Test against Australia in Darwin, having produced an impressive all-round performance over the first three days.
The Tigers bowled Australia out for 198 in the first innings and secured a massive 228-run lead. By the end of the third day, they had reduced the hosts to 161 for four.
Australia currently trails by 67 runs with six wickets remaining. While they have a fighting chance, analysts suggest their win probability is around 15 per cent.
Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto emphasized that the team is focusing on the process and session-by-session play rather than the outcome.
For Australia, Cameron Green (43*) and Alex Carey (19*) are the key hopes for a comeback. Alyssa Healy believes a big score from Green could give Australia a real shot at victory.
Bangladesh will look to maintain their disciplined approach to secure a historic win in the ගොඩක් ගොඩක් ගොඩින් Darwin Test.
caption:

Australia currently trails by 67 runs with six wickets remaining. While they have a fighting chance, analysts suggest their win probability is around 15 per cent.

Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto emphasized that the team is focusing on the process and session-by-session play rather than the outcome.

For Australia, Cameron Green (43*) and Alex Carey (19*) are the key hopes for a comeback. Alyssa Healy believes a big score from Green could give Australia a real shot at victory.

headline: 902 children dead as measles outbreak kills 8 more in 24 hours
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services reports a surge in measles-like symptoms, with total suspected and confirmed deaths crossing 900 this year.
details: Eight children died with measles-like symptoms in the last 24 hours, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
This brings the total number of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths in Bangladesh to 902 for the current year.
The DGHS has classified the eight most recent fatalities as suspected measles deaths.
Nationwide, the total number of suspected measles cases has reached 141,776, with 728 new suspected cases reported in the last 24 hours.
Laboratory-confirmed infections have reached 17,800, with 70 new confirmed cases recorded in the last day.
Since March 15, a total of 123,494 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalized across the country.
Of those hospitalized, 119,089 patients have recovered, according to the latest DGHS data.
